Seminar Title:

Design and Analysis of In-Band Full-Duplex Antenna Systems with Enhanced SIC for future 6G Applications

Seminar Type:

Progress Seminar

Department:

Electronics and Communication Engineering

Speaker Name:

Amrit Prasad Behera ( Rollno : 524ec1002)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

EC 303

Date and Time:

14 Oct 2026 9 am to 10 am

Contact:

Jogesh Chandra Dash

Abstract:

The growing demand for high-speed wireless communication and the resulting spectrum scarcity present
critical bottlenecks for next-generation networks, driving strong interest in in-band full-duplex (IBFD) systems.
By enabling simultaneous transmission and reception on the same frequency band, IBFD technology effectively
doubles spectral efficiency, reduces latency, and unlocks key cross-domain capabilities, such as integrated sensing
and communication (ISAC), simultaneous uplink/downlink in dense IoT, and aggressive spectral reuse in 6G
backhaul and compact airborne platforms. However, the primary obstacle to realizing these benefits is selfinterference
(SI), where high-power transmit signals leak into the receiver chain and mask weak incoming
signals.
This report presents the design, analysis, and evaluation of advanced IBFD microstrip antenna architectures
engineered to achieve high antenna-domain self-interference cancellation (SIC) within compact footprints.
Techniques including shorted-microstrip-line (SML) structures, integrated metallic vias, and modified stubs embedded
in shared-radiator configurations are investigated to deliver strong port isolation and robust impedance
matching. The operational mechanisms of the proposed structures are validated through full-wave electromagnetic
simulations, equivalent circuit modeling, and experimental measurements on fabricated prototypes. Furthermore,
system-level communications performance is verified using software-defined radio (SDR) platforms.
Overall, the proposed antenna designs offer compact, low-complexity, and high-isolation solutions well-suited
for space-constrained, dual-band, and multi-band applications in future 6G wireless networks.
